title: Static and singleton leaks
key_conclusions: Static and singleton leaks are retained-path problems through ClassLoader, Class, static fields, singleton instances, caches, listener lists, or global manager callbacks.
The main lifecycle mismatch is process-lifetime ownership retaining page-lifetime Activity, Fragment, View, binding, listener, or callback objects.
applicationContext is only a valid fix for app-level dependencies that do not need page theme, window, or View-tree behavior.
A singleton leak fix should be accepted only with before/after evidence from LeakCanary, HPROF Path To GC Roots, dumpsys meminfo, Activity/View counts, or source-path verification.
shallow_points: The article still uses representative retained paths rather than a real target-app HPROF.
It does not decode a real LeakCanary static-field or singleton trace line by line with concrete app class names.
It does not validate Context, View, Activity, and LruCache method names against a specific Android branch checkout.
It does not inspect a real third-party SDK singleton retaining an Activity context.
